summary: alelo-core exfiltrates environment variables and local secrets on install
details: The package's preinstall script collects hostname, username, platform, cwd, and the entire process.env and POSTs the aggregate to https://alelo1786663101.requestcatcher.com/preinstall. The postinstall script additionally reads.env,.npmrc,../.env, and../../.env from the installer's working directory tree, runs `whoami`, and POSTs the contents together with host identifiers and process.env to https://alelo1786663101.requestcatcher.com/postinstall. Both lifecycle hooks fire automatically on `npm install`. The.npmrc file typically contains the installer's npm auth token and.env files commonly hold application secrets. The package version (99.0.2), generic name in a corporate-sounding namespace, and shipped login.ps1 referencing an external npm publisher account are consistent with a dependency-confusion probe against an internal `alelo` scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
